STEP 1 - Scene: A close-up overhead photo of scrambled eggs (or a similar soft-cooked egg dish) on a white square plate. Only this plate is the meal; no other foods are part of it.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square plate, roughly 22-24 cm across. Using ~22 cm diameter-equivalent: area = 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2. (The plate appears square, so this is an approximation.)

STEP 3 - Items: Scrambled eggs (pale yellow, soft curds, some slightly firmer pieces). No visible oil, sauce, or garnish beyond a faint sheen.

STEP 4 - Area: Scrambled eggs cover roughly 22% of the plate area (the pile spans a region about 14 cm x 10 cm, with gaps). 22% of 380 cm^2 ≈ 84 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: 84 cm^2 x ~2 cm typical height ≈ 168 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: 168 ml x 0.95 g/ml (dense egg curds) ≈ 160 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Scrambled egg, cooked, with a little butter or oil typical of preparation, ≈ 150 kcal per 100 g (plain scrambled egg ~149 kcal; added fat raises it, but no added fat is clearly visible, so I use ~150). 160 g x 1.5 = 240 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small mound of scrambled eggs covering about a fifth of a plate, roughly 160 g and about 240 kcal, is plausible for a single serving of two to three eggs.

**Estimate: about 160 g, about 240 kcal.**
